name: clock_skew__stamp_freshness
regression: Jetson/robot clock skew fooling freshness: with stamp-based freshness a skewed publisher clock keeps a dead command 'fresh' for 1.5 s longer. HELIX P10 forbids stamp-based freshness for this reason; the monitor judges on receipt time and catches it (GO2 field notes: robot stamps read a 2025 date during a 2026 session; payload has no RTC).
initial_conditions: Synthetic GO2 + HELIX run (6.5 s): /nav/cmd_vel at 20 Hz commands 0 m/s, then 0.15 m/s from t=2 s; HELIX hold published at 10 Hz, never asserted; odometry and lowstate at 20 Hz from the robot host, whose clock is 1.734 s ahead of the payload.
injected_fault: The command publisher's clock runs 1.5 s ahead of the arbiter host for the whole run, and /nav/cmd_vel stops at t=4.0 s. The arbiter is configured (counterfactually) to judge freshness by DDS source timestamps.
